Record what a render published

Source: R/study_render_commit.R
study_render_record.Rd

Adds a render record to this copy's render ref, tying every output a render published to the commit its figures print. Records accumulate, so a figure copied into a manuscript can be traced after its job is rendered again.

Usage

study_render_record(
  render_id,
  commit,
  job,
  outputs,
  extra = list(),
  root = study_root()
)

Arguments

render_id

Character(1). The render's identifier; names the record.

commit

Character(1). The commit from study_render_commit that the outputs print.

job

Character(1). The job rendered, relative to the study root.

outputs

Character. Paths of the published files, absolute or relative to the study root; each must exist.

extra

List. Further fields for the record. Default list().

root

Character(1). The study root. Default study_root().

Value

Invisibly, the record as a list.

Details

The record is written as .hvti-renders/<render_id>.json in a new commit on the render ref, and every later render commit carries it, so the ref's tip holds every record. It names commit, job, the time, extra (typically the render's provenance) and, for each file in outputs, its path relative to the study root and its sha256. A render that fails should publish nothing and record nothing.

See also

study_render_commit

Examples

# \donttest{
if (nzchar(Sys.which("git"))) {
  root <- file.path(tempdir(), "render-record-example")
  study_setup(root, "Render record example", 1L, renv = FALSE)
  writeLines("fit <- 1", file.path(root, "30_analyses", "fit.R"))
  writeLines("figure", file.path(root, "30_analyses", "fit.png"))
  withr::with_envvar(c(
    GIT_AUTHOR_NAME = "Example", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL = "example@example.org",
    GIT_COMMITTER_NAME = "Example", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL = "example@example.org"
  ), {
    sha <- study_render_commit("30_analyses/fit.R", root = root)
    rec <- study_render_record("r1", sha, "30_analyses/fit.R",
                               "30_analyses/fit.png", root = root)
    print(rec$outputs)
  })
  unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
}
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$path
#> [1] "30_analyses/fit.png"
#> 
#> [[1]]$sha256
#> [1] "e952f88f5e35916f10eb0b1495710c1dec05ddd468e23d22afedcb934e2e46cb"
#>
